L215: # Definition of 'enemy'
L216: 
L217: COBUILD frequency band
L218: ## enemy
L219: 
L220: (e nəmi )
L221: 
L222: Word forms: plural enemies
L223: 
L224: 1. countable noun 【40†B1+†blog.collinsdictionary.com】
L225: 
L226: If someone is your enemy, they 【41†hate】 you or 【42†want】 to harm you.
L227: 
L228: 2. countable noun 【40†B1+†blog.collinsdictionary.com】
L229: 
L230: If someone is your enemy, they are opposed to you and to what you 【43†think】 or do.
L231: 
L232: The Government's political enemies were quick to pick up on this series of disasters.
L233: 
L234: 3. singular noun [with singular or plural verb, NOUN noun] 【40†B2†blog.collinsdictionary.com】
L235: The enemy is an 【44†army】 or other force that is opposed to you in a war, or a country with which your country is at war.
L236: 
L237: The enemy were pursued for two miles.
L238: 
L239: He searched the skies for enemy bombers.
L240: 
L241: 4. countable noun [usually singular]
L242: 
L243: If one thing is the enemy of another thing, the second thing cannot 【45†happen】 or 【46†succeed】 because of the first thing.
L244: 
L245: [formal]
L246: 
L247: Reform, as we know, is the enemy of revolution. 【47†[+ of]†grammar.collinsdictionary.com】
L248:

L278: ## enemy in British English
L279: 
L280: (ˈɛnəmɪ )
L281: 
L282: noun Word forms: plural -mies
L283: 
L284: 1.
L285: 
L286: a person 【57†hostile】 or opposed to a 【58†policy】, cause, person, or group, esp one who actively 【59†tries】 to do 【60†damage】; 【61†opponent】
L287: 
L288: 2.
L289: 
L290: a.
L291: 
L292: an armed 【62†adversary】; opposing military force
L293: 
L294: b.
L295: 
L296: (as modifier)
L297: 
L298: enemy aircraft
L299: 
L300: 3.
L301: 
L302: a.
L303: 
L304: a hostile 【63†nation】 or people
L305: 
L306: b.
L307: 
L308: (as modifier)
L309: 
L310: an enemy alien
L311: 
L312: 4.
L313: 
L314: something that 【64†harms】 or opposes; adversary
L315: 
L316: courage is the enemy of failure
L317: 
L318: ▶ Related adjective: inimical

L323: C13: from Old French enemi, from Latin inimīcus hostile, from in-1 + amīcus friend

L328: ## enemy in American English
L329: 
L330: (ˈɛnəmi )
L331: 
L332: noun Word forms: plural enemies Origin: ME & OFr enemi < L inimicus, unfriendly, enemy < in-, not + amicus, friend: see 【65†amiable】
L333: 
L334: 1.
L335: 
L336: a person who hates another, and 【66†wishes】 or tries to 【67†injure】 him or her; 【68†foe】
L337: 
L338: 2.
L339: 
L340: a.
L341: 
L342: a nation or force hostile to another; military or 【69†wartime】 adversary
L343: 
L344: b.
L345: 
L346: 【70†troops】, 【71†fleet】, ship, member, etc. of a hostile nation
L347: 
L348: 3.
L349: 
L350: a person hostile to an 【72†idea】, cause, etc.

L215: # Definition of 'ally'
L216: 
L217: COBUILD frequency band
L218: ## ally
L219: 
L220: æ laɪ (noun), əl aɪ (verb)
L221: 
L222: Word forms: plural allies , 3rd person singular present tense allies , present participle allying , past tense, past participle allied pronunciation note:   The noun is pronounced (æ laɪ ). The verb is pronounced (əl aɪ ).
L223: 
L224: 1. countable noun
L225: 
L226: A country's ally is another country that has an 【41†agreement】 to support it, 【42†especially】 in war.
L227: 
L228: Washington would not take such a step without its allies' approval.
L229: It was assumed that Germany would not want to bring such a powerful ally of Britain into the war. 【43†[+ of]†grammar.collinsdictionary.com】
L230: 
L231: 2. plural noun
L232: 
L233: The Allies were the armed forces that 【44†fought】 against Germany and 【45†Japan】 in the Second World War.
L234: 
L235: 3. countable noun
L236: 
L237: If you 【46†describe】 someone as your ally, you mean that they 【47†help】 and support you, especially when other people are opposing you.
L238: 
L239: He is a close ally of the Prime Minister. 【43†[+ of]†grammar.collinsdictionary.com】
L240: She will regret losing a close political ally.
L241: 
L242: Synonyms: 【48†partner】, 【49†friend】, 【50†colleague】, 【51†associate】   【52†More Synonyms of ally】
L243: 
L244: 4. countable noun
L245: 
L246: An ally is someone who supports people who are in a 【53†minority】 group or who are 【54†discriminated】 against, 【55†even】 though they do not belong to that group themselves.
L247: 
L248: So step up as an ally to the LGBT people around you at work. 【56†[+ to]†grammar.collinsdictionary.com】
L249: 
L250: 5. verb
L251: If you ally yourself with someone or something, you give your support to them.
L252: 
L253: He will have no choice but to ally himself with the new movement. [VERB pronoun-reflexive + with]
L254: 
L255: Synonyms: 【57†combine】, 【58†unite】, 【59†join】, 【60†link】   【52†More Synonyms of ally】
L256: 
L257: 6.  See also 【61†allied】
L258:

L215: # Definition of 'neutral'
L216: 
L217: COBUILD frequency band
L218: ## neutral
L219: 
L220: (nj uː trəl , US n uː t- )
L221: 
L222: Word forms: plural neutrals
L223: 
L224: 1. adjective
L225: 
L226: If a person or country 【40†adopts】 a neutral position or remains neutral, they do not support anyone in a 【41†disagreement】, war, or 【42†contest】.
L227: 
L228: Let's meet on neutral territory.
L229: 
L230: Those who had tried to remain neutral now found themselves required to take sides. 【43†[+ in]†grammar.collinsdictionary.com】
L231: 
L232: Synonyms: 【44†unbiased】, 【45†impartial】, 【46†disinterested】, 【47†even-handed】   【48†More Synonyms of neutral】
L233: countable noun
L234: 
L235: A neutral is someone who is neutral.
L236: 
L237: It was a good game to watch for the neutrals.
L238: 
L239: neutrality (njuːtr æ lɪti , US nuːt- ) uncountable noun
L240: 
L241: ...a reputation for political neutrality and impartiality.
L242: 
L243: Synonyms: impartiality, 【49†detachment】, noninterference, disinterestedness   【50†More Synonyms of neutral】
L244: 
L245: 2. adjective [usually ADJECTIVE noun]
L246: 
L247: If someone speaks in a neutral voice or if the expression on their face is neutral, they do not show what they are 【51†thinking】 or feeling.
L248: Isabel put her magazine down and said in a neutral voice, 'You're very late, darling.'
L249: 
L250: He told her about the death, describing the events in as neutral a manner as he could.
L251: 
L252: Synonyms: 【52†expressionless】, 【53†dull】, 【54†blank】, 【55†deadpan】   【48†More Synonyms of neutral】
L253: 
L254: neutrality uncountable noun
L255: 
L256: I noticed, behind the neutrality of his gaze, a deep weariness. 【56†[+ of]†grammar.collinsdictionary.com】
L257: 
L258: 3. adjective
L259: If you 【57†say】 that something is neutral, you mean that it does not have any effect on other things because it lacks any 【58†significant】 qualities of its own, or it is an equal 【59†balance】 of two or more different qualities, amounts, or ideas.
L260: 
L261: Three in every five interviewed felt that the Budget was neutral and they would be no better off.
L262: 
L263: 4. graded adjective
L264: 
L265: If someone uses neutral language, they 【60†choose】 words which do not indicate that they 【61†approve】 or 【62†disapprove】 of something.
L266: Both sides had agreed to use neutral terms in their references to each other.
L267: 
L268: He had departed from his prepared testimony, which was considered to be neutral.
L269: 
L270: 5. uncountable noun [oft into/in N]
L271: 
L272: Neutral is the position between the 【63†gears】 of a vehicle such as a car, in which the gears are not connected to the engine.
L273: 
L274: Graham put the van in neutral and jumped out into the road.
L275: 
L276: 6. adjective
L277: In an electrical device or system, the neutral wire is one of the three wires needed to complete the circuit so that the current can flow. The other two wires are called the earth wire and the live or 【64†positive】 wire.
L278: 
L279: 7. colour
L280: 
L281: Neutral is used to 【65†describe】 things that have a 【66†pale】 colour such as 【67†cream】 or grey, or that have no colour at all.
L282: 
L283: At the horizon the land mass becomes a continuous pale neutral grey.
L284: 
L285: Mary suggests using a neutral lip pencil.
L286: 
L287: 8. adjective
L288: In 【68†physics】, neutral is used to describe things such as atomic particles that have neither a positive nor a 【69†negative】 charge.
L289: 
L290: A neutron is simply a neutral particle in the nucleus of an atom.
L291: 
L292: 9. adjective
L293: 
L294: In 【70†chemistry】, neutral is used to describe things that are neither acid nor alkaline.
L295: 
L296: Pure water is neutral with a pH of 7.
L297:
